--- title: "[CensoringType]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-enum}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} The type of a `Surv` response, using R's type names. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_surv.py#L60-L195){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python CensoringType() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} - `RIGHT`: right-censored, `Surv(time, event)`. - `LEFT`: left-censored, `Surv(time, event, type="left")`. - `INTERVAL`: interval-censored, from `type="interval"` or `type="interval2"`. - `COUNTING`: counting-process `(start, stop]` intervals, `Surv(start, stop, event)`. - `MRIGHT`: multi-state right-censored, from a categorical `event=`. - `MCOUNTING`: multi-state counting-process, from a categorical `event=` with start times. A response reports its type through `Surv(...).type`. Because `CensoringType` is a `str` enum, it compares equal to R's type strings, such as `"right"`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#58b9e5e1 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from greenwood import CensoringType list(CensoringType) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [, , , , , ] ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes}
